previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 34-year-old woman with sickle cell disease was admitted for a severe pain crisis involving her limbs and joints, following weeks of worsening pain managed at home with limited success. She presented somnolent due to prior sedation but stabilized after 18 hours of rest and continuous IV pain control with Dilaudid, ketorolac, and fluids. A chest X-ray ruled out acute chest syndrome or infection, and labs showed no evidence of acute complications. Over several days, she transitioned successfully to oral hydromorphone and was discharged home in stable condition. Her hydroxyurea dose was maintained at 500 mg twice daily, considering her underlying Hepatitis C with stage III fibrosis. Follow-up was advised for pain management and hematologic care.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma

chest and lower extremity pain were thought to be the result of

hydroxyurea and folic acid.  For pain, the patient received 
Torodal and IV Dilaudid.  MS ___ SR, taken at bedtime, was

patient's hematocrit was monitored throughout the patient's 
admission and remained stable after an initial drop. The patient 
did not require any blood transfusions.

discharge. She was afebrile and satting well on room air at the

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___

Comparison made with prior study from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Sickle cell disease, presenting with crisis.  Evaluate for
pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral views of the chest are obtained.  There is a stable
appearance of the lungs with mild prominence of the interstitial markings
which appear similar to multiple prior exams.  There is no superimposed
pneumonia or CHF.  No pleural effusion or pneumothorax is seen.
Cardiomediastinal silhouette is stable with mild cardiac enlargement again
noted.  Osseous structures are unchanged with concave-appearing endplates in
the thoracic spine, compatible with sickle cell disease and H-shaped
vertebrae. No free air is seen below the right hemidiaphragm.

IMPRESSION:  Stable exam with persistent interstitial prominence and mild
cardiac enlargement.  No superimposed pneumonia or CHF.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with sickle cell disease, fever, nonproductive
cough and rhinorrhea.

COMPARISONS:  Prior studies since ___ including prior day.

CHEST, PORTABLE AP UPRIGHT:  There is similar prominence of the main pulmonary
artery.  The cardiac and mediastinal contours are unchanged.  A baseline
interstitial abnormality appears unchanged since a prior portable radiograph
from ___, which provides a good comparison, but since the prior day,
there are increased left lower lobe opacities, including minimal elevation of
the left hemidiaphragm suggestive of slight volume loss.

IMPRESSION:  New left lower lobe opacity.  Given its rapid onset and
suggestion of volume loss, atelectasis is an important differential
consideration, but the possibility of pneumonia cannot be excluded.
Radiographic followup is recommended.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Sickle cell crisis, febrile, left lower lobe opacity identified
on the portable chest x-ray.  Followup.

radiograph is unchanged.
